title: Bavarian Long COVID Registry: a Bavarian registry for Long COVID and Long COVID-like diseases
summary:
The Bavarian Long COVID Registry (BAY-LCR) is a medical data collection of patients who are being treated for Long COVID or Long COVID-like conditions at the participating Bavarian centers and who have agreed to participate in the registry. 
Long COVID refers to symptoms that persist four weeks after the initial infection with the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Studies show that about 10–30% of those infected with SARS-CoV-2 are affected by Long COVID, though the numbers in these studies vary widely. The most common symptoms of Long COVID include fatigue and exhaustion, reduced tolerance for everyday tasks, respiratory problems, concentration difficulties, and cardiovascular issues. Often, the quality of life, education, and/or work capacity of those affected is impaired, and they may be confined to their home or bedridden.
The BAY-LC registry aims to create a reliable medical data collection for clinical, translational, and care-oriented studies in order to answer specific questions within these studies. The BAY-LCR thus serves to improve research, care, and health policy management of Long COVID and ensures a better long-term understanding of the disease as well as better treatment for those affected by Long COVID.
conditions: COVID-19 vaccines causing adverse effects in therapeutic use, unspecified

interventions.name: Multicenter Registry: Epidemiological, medical, and care-related data of patients with Long COVID and Long COVID-like conditions are collected as part of their routine clinical care at a participating center and stored in a web-based registry.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Written and/or digital consent from the patients or, in the case of children and adolescents, written and/or digital assent from the patients and written and/or digital consent from their legal guardians. 
2) Standardized diagnostics at a medical facility specialized in Long COVID due to Long COVID-like symptoms.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Within 3 months after digital consent, no written confirmation of the consent by the patient or by a guardian (if applicable, also on behalf of the other guardian) is provided on-site at the care center or by mail.  
2) The consent is withdrawn.
